bullets: Un sistema rápido cruza el lunes con humedad y dinámica limitadas: solo chubascos ligeros y acumulaciones mínimas en terreno alto.
Una cresta de alta presión trae tiempo seco desde el martes hasta al menos media semana.
Para Thanksgiving y el fin de semana sigue posible un patrón más activo, pero los ensambles no coinciden (confianza baja).

news.summary: No hay anuncios ni reportes de trabajos de apertura en los Back Bowls. Vail abrió la temporada el 13 de noviembre con terreno limitado y el pronóstico solo trae nevadas ligeras esta semana.

sections.Key Messages:
- Mild and dry conditions expected through Thanksgiving.
- There is increasing confidence in active weather for the
  holiday weekend after Thanksgiving with the northern mountains
  being favored for snowfall. Exact details remain uncertain at
  this time. Stay tuned for updates to timing and impacts as
  they become available especially if traveling.
- An unsettled pattern looks to continue into next week with
  potential for more mountain snow but details remain uncertain.
sections.Discussion:
Issued at 1031 AM MST Wed Nov 25 2026
MILD AND DRY CONDITIONS THROUGH THANKSGIVING:
A shortwave ridge moving overhead will lead to dry and mild
afternoon conditions. Upstream, high clouds continue to
infiltrate across the area as a shortwave approaches from the
west. All indications continue to point towards a split flow
pattern with a closed low passing well south of Arizona and New
Mexico, leaving us with just some passing mid and high cloud
cover this evening into Thanksgiving morning with thin high
clouds Thanksgiving Day and pleasant mild and dry conditions
with temperatures around 5 to 10 degrees above normal. Some low
level moisture with the colder nights may lead to patchy fog
development overnight especially where clearing skies occur but
low confidence due to passing cloud cover which would make this
less likely.
POTENTIAL SYSTEM AFTER THANKSGIVING INTO THE WEEKEND:
Beyond Thanksgiving Day, moisture will begin moving into the
Pacific Northwest and across the northern Rockies Friday into
the weekend, setting up a northwest flow across the region as
high pressure builds over the Desert Southwest just off the
SoCal coast. The Park Range looks to receive the brunt of this
moisture with a favored set up for northwest orographic snowfall
Friday through Saturday, but more particularly Friday evening
through Saturday night. While confidence is high that a weather
system will impact the region, there are still some
discrepancies on how far south the impacts will extend based on
varying model solutions. We could see impacts down to Vail Pass
especially into Saturday as a stronger piece of energy pushes
through on the back side of the trough, but the Park Range
looks to benefit the most from decent snow accumulations from
this northwest orographic flow. Confidence is highest over the
Park Range with lowering confidence to the south. Highlights
may be needed but would like to see some better clarification on
details before issuing any products depending on timing and
amounts. Anyone traveling late this week and this weekend
should prepare for potentially difficult conditions.
LOOKING AHEAD TO NEXT WEEK:
High pressure ridge moves back in for Sunday following the
passage of this system with northwest flow setting up again on
Monday as a weak clipper brushes to the north. There is a chance
that northwest orographic flow could keep snow ongoing over the
Park Range so this remains to be seen. Looking ahead, there are
some indications of another system impacting the region mid to
late next week but guidance diverges on specific scenarios.
Regardless, it looks to remain unsettled.
